thread.text:
Most browser driving games fake drifting with a lateral slide variable and a handbrake key.

We built an endless EV drifting game using real weight-transfer physics and throttle balance—running entirely inside a single zero-dependency HTML file.

Here is how the physics and audio engine work 🧵👇
thread.mediaNote: GIF/Video: Smooth entry drift through a biome transition, showing EV cockpit HUD gauges reacting dynamically.

thread.text:
1/ True Weight-Transfer Dynamics (No Handbrake)

Oversteer is triggered by trail-braking: decelerating pitches mass forward, lightening rear tire load. 

Throttle feeds instant EV torque to sustain the slide, and counter-steering catches the snap. We even verified physics invariants via headless Chrome CDP tests.
thread.mediaNote: Diagram or telemetry clip showing front/rear axle load distribution during turn entry and slip-angle calculation.

thread.text:
2/ Zero-Asset Procedural WebAudio Synth

There are zero audio files loaded over the network. The electric motor is fully synthesized via WebAudio:

• Oscillator pitch = real-time wheel speed
• Gain/loudness = absolute kW output
• Harmonic sub-waves bend downward during regenerative braking
thread.mediaNote: Short video clip with sound enabled showing instant audio response during acceleration, hard regen braking, and high-speed drift.

thread.text:
3/ Why Single-File Web Apps Feel Magical

No npm install. No 50MB WebAssembly blobs. No 15-second loading screens.

Just raw Vanilla JS and Canvas2D rendering 4 biomes, zombie bounties, and deterministic daily ghost runs at 60fps in under 0.1s load time.
